the induction of CAM in C. minor is associated with the decarboxylation of citrate, which occurs in parallel with malate decarboxylation, but is not directly linked to the photoinhibition of PSII.

CAM induction in Clusias is associated with a seasonal decline in leaf water status, a reduction in day-time photosynthesis, a concomitant increase in the diurnal turnover of organic acids and a reduction in the photoinhibitory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the diel turnover and decarboxylative fate of malate and/or citrate are closely coupled and that the diel pattern of CAM induction in Clusias is driven by a combination of factors, including photoinhibition, leaf water status and the availability of organic acids.
the induction of CAM in Clusia is not a simple response to the onset of water stress.
the induction of CAM in C. minor during the transition from the wet season to dry season in tropical Trinidad is associated with the accumulation of both malic and citric acid.
